- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). Work, the consumer, still does not advance on such a result: a read-only result carrying `read-only-mutation-correlated` or `mutated-dirty-before-correlated` (or, read back from disk, a non-empty `evidence.changedFiles`/`mutatedDirtyBeforeFiles`, since stored warnings are as writable as any other field) stops with its own reason `assignment--correlated-mutation` (at planning: `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`), never folded into no-evidence; a round that failed on its own terms (non-zero exit, a timeout settles as 124; a policy refusal, a proven write among them; a provider, resource or contract failure) keeps `assignment--failed`. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`. - **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it. Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers..accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker and panel roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11).

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined).
